products.name: Workday AI
products.note: HR and finance AI; skills-based talent; predictive analytics; sensitive HR data exposure

profile_text.body:
Workday is a publicly traded enterprise software company, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Pleasanton, California, that offers cloud-based applications for human resources, finance, and IT management. The company trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker WDAY and reported revenue of approximately $9.552 billion for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026.

The company describes its platform as an enterprise AI system for HR, finance, and IT, and positions its core AI product, Workday AI, around agentic capabilities, skills-based talent management, predictive analytics, and automated workflows. The site highlights a product called Sana alongside what it characterizes as agentic AI that can "find, build, act, and automate" across business functions. The site frames this as moving beyond simple assistance toward AI systems that can independently execute key processes in HR, finance, and IT.

The held facts note nine federal lawsuits filed against Workday across multiple district courts, including cases in the Eastern and Northern Districts of California, the Northern District of Georgia, the District of Colorado, the District of Maryland, and the Eastern District of Virginia. The site's records indicate 175 instances of California law exposure associated with the company. The nature of these cases is not specified in the available data beyond their court filings and party names.
